title: Verifying Proper Function of the Aerosol Evacuation System Prior to Sorting Infectious Samples
author: Reifel, Aspland, et al.

Some manufacturers have developed instrument‐specific protocols for this test that recommend particular sheath pressures and/or event rates (e.g., Thermo Fisher Scientific, 2024). In these cases, it is recommended to follow the manufacturer's instructions. Alternatively, the highest possible sheath pressure and event rate for the instrument model can be used if less than 70 psi and 50,000 events/s, respectively, or the highest sheath pressure used for all laboratory protocols can be used. Results of the test are valid for all sheath pressures equal to or less than the tested sheath pressure. If higher sheath pressures will be used, the test must be repeated at the maximum sheath pressure to verify the higher aerosol load is contained by the aerosol evacuation system and engineering controls. Nozzle size is likely to have a smaller effect on the concentration and/or size distribution of aerosols, but these effects have not been characterized. We suggest using the same nozzle size typically used for cell sorting to best approximate aerosols that would be released during a stream deviation. In general, sensitivity can be increased by collecting a larger volume of air in the test sample (without exceeding the manufacturer's recommendations), which decreases the detection limit and, to a lesser extent, by running the bead sample at a higher event rate to increase the proportion of aerosols that contains a bead. Note that collecting smaller volumes of air (e.g., shortening collection time of the test sample) will increase the detection limit and reduce the sensitivity of the test.

steps.title: Gather all required materials
steps.instruction: Collect disposable aerosol sampler cassette (d50 ≈1 µm, capacity ≥200 L), vacuum pump with rotameter set to the cassette‑specified airflow, compatible tubing, cassette holder or stand, timer (up to ~20 min, 1 s resolution), cell sorter, 1‑µm Dragon Green fluorescent beads (or equivalent), buffer (PBS with 0.1 % sodium azide and 0.5 % Tween 20), optional reference beads, disposable microscope slides (gridded preferred), immersion oil or mounting medium, epifluorescence microscope (excitation ~480 nm, emission ~520 nm), spray bottle or other aerosolizer, and optional negative‑control collection equipment.

steps.title: Prepare reference slide (optional)
steps.instruction: Using a cover slip from an identical cassette, apply the collected aerosol sample to the adhesive side, mount on a disposable slide, add immersion oil if desired, and label as reference for microscope setup.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescent bead solution
steps.instruction: In a microcentrifuge tube combine 20 µL of 1‑µm Dragon Green beads (Bangs Laboratories, cat. no. FSDG004) with 2 mL PBS containing 0.1 % sodium azide and 0.5 % Tween 20. Mix gently, store at 4 °C for up to 2 days, and use fresh for each test. Set the sorter flow rate (typically 3 or 4) to achieve an event rate of 50 000–55 000 events / s.

steps.title: Collect negative‑control sample (optional)
steps.instruction: With the aerosol evacuation system on and no bead aerosol generated, run the sampler cassette for 15–20 min to capture ambient debris. This can be done before or after instrument startup.

steps.title: Set sorter sheath pressure and event rate
steps.instruction: Adjust the cell sorter to a sheath pressure of 70 psi (or the highest pressure allowed by the instrument) and a total event rate of ~50 000 events / s (or the highest rate feasible). Use the same nozzle size normally employed for sorting.

steps.title: Position aerosol sampler cassette(s)
steps.instruction: Place each cassette just outside the sort collection area, as close as possible to the door edge where aerosols may escape. Secure the cassette with a stand, retort holder, or tape. Connect the cassette to the vacuum pump via appropriate tubing and set the pump airflow to the manufacturer‑recommended rate (checked with the rotameter).

steps.title: Activate aerosol evacuation system for test sample
steps.instruction: Turn on the integrated (Option A) or external (Option B) aerosol evacuation system. Verify that all containment controls are engaged (doors closed, waste‑drain vacuums on).

steps.title: Generate test aerosol and collect air sample
steps.instruction: Using a spray bottle or other aerosolizer, continuously spray the prepared bead solution into the sorter’s stream to create a high‑concentration aerosol while the sorter runs at the settings defined above. Collect air through the cassette until the specified volume of 200 L has been sampled (monitor with the pump’s flow indicator or timer; collection time will be ≤20 min).

steps.title: Collect positive‑control sample
steps.instruction: Turn off the aerosol evacuation system. With the same cassette placement, repeat the aerosol generation using the bead solution. Collect air for a short defined period (e.g., 2 min) aiming to capture ≥100 beads on the cassette (tolerance set to ≥100 beads). If bead counts are excessively high or liquid is visible, reduce the collection time or move the cassette farther from the door.

steps.title: Allow air turnover before further work
steps.instruction: If additional sampling is required after the positive control, wait 30–60 min (depending on room or BSC air‑exchange rate) before proceeding.

steps.title: Retrieve cassettes and prepare microscope slides
steps.instruction: Remove each cassette, carefully detach the adhesive cover slip containing the collected particles, place it onto a disposable microscope slide, add a drop of immersion oil or mounting medium, cover with a coverslip, and label appropriately.

steps.title: Examine slides and record bead counts
steps.instruction: Using an epifluorescence microscope set to the bead’s excitation (≈480 nm) and emission (≈520 nm) wavelengths, locate the grid, focus on the adhesive surface, and count fluorescent beads. Verify that the test sample contains zero beads and that the positive‑control sample contains ≥100 beads. Use the optional reference slide to aid identification of beads versus background debris.

steps.title: Document results
steps.instruction: Enter instrument information, material lot numbers, sorter settings, cassette placement, collection volumes, and bead counts into the designated report sheet (see Figure 10). Keep the report for quality‑control records.

steps.title: Clean work area
steps.instruction: Thoroughly clean laboratory floors, benchtop surfaces, and any equipment that may have been exposed to bead aerosol (e.g., spray bottle, tubing) using appropriate cleaning agents to prevent future false‑positive results.

description: In this protocol, proper containment and evacuation of cell sorter‐derived aerosols by the aerosol evacuation system are assessed by running a sample of 1‐µm fluorescent beads while purposefully generating aerosols, a proportion of which will contain beads. Air samples are then collected just outside the enclosed sort collection area in an effort to detect the beads. The fluorescent beads are used to identify cell sorter‐derived aerosols and distinguish them from background. At least one test sample and one positive control sample must be collected. Additional samples can be collected as desired (see Critical Parameters and Understanding Results). Note that some manufacturers have developed protocols to perform this test on specific cell sorter models. In these cases, follow the manufacturer's instructions for instrument settings and placement of cassettes. See Table 1 for a troubleshooting guide with suggestions and recommendations for addressing potential issues and unexpected results that can occur when implementing this procedure.
